steps: dlg | Bailiff CraneEdric's heir. Bailiff Crane, of the Crown. Item: forty-one things to list before Midwinter, and I shall be thorough about every one. Walk with me.1Walk with you | choose | 1Walk with you
dlg | Bailiff CraneNow the other column, the one people prefer not to read. I brought the papers myself.1Show me | choose | 1Show me
dlg | Bailiff CraneBefore I stamp it, heir: do you own more than you owe, or less?1More2Less | choose | 1More
dlg | Bailiff CraneLess. Much less, and I am required to say it plainly.1Next | choose | 1Next
dlg | Bailiff CraneThe writ requires a name for the land. Item: what shall I write?1Give it a name | choose | 1Give it a name
dlg | Bailiff CraneItem: Thornfield. Entered on the writ, and not to be changed without a form.1Next | choose | 1Next

dlg | Bailiff CraneI am instructed to convey an offer from Corvin Vane for Thornfield. Item: 300, in coin, today. I do not recommend it.1No. The farm stays.2Sell Thornfield for 300 | choose | 1No. The farm stays.
dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡That was Crane. Don't mind him: he counts everything twice because he's frightened of nearly everything.1Next | choose | 1Next
dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡What you own minus what you owe is yours, and yours is below zero. That's why we work.1Next | choose | 1Next
dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡Profit is an opinion. Cash is a fact.1Next | choose | 1Next

dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡Right. You said 33.Markup is profit ÷ cost, 50%. Margin is profit ÷ price, 50 ÷ 150 = 33%. Same sale, two numbers.1Next | choose | 1Next

dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡Two kinds of cost: variable (seed and grain, rising with every sack) and fixed (wages and interest, due every week whatever you sold). This week's fixed bill is 48.1Next | choose | 1Next
dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡A sack at 8 leaves 4 after its 4 of grain: its contribution. Break-even is the sacks whose contribution covers the fixed bill: 48 ÷ 4 = 12 sacks a week.1Next | choose | 1Next

dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡Suppose a rival like Grisby sets up and undercuts you: the going price falls to 6, a cut of 25%. How many sacks a week do you need to break even now?1About 242About 12 (a small cut changes little)3About 15 | choose | 1About 24
dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡Yes. The contribution fell from 4 to 2, down 50%, but the fixed bill did not move.1Next | choose | 1Next

dlg | Maud the reeve♥♡♡♡♡So break-even rose from 12 to 24 sacks, up 100%. A small price cut is a big cut in contribution, which is why a rival's undercut hurts more than it looks.1Next | choose | 1Next
panel | pgok | Edric's letter: Maud's calendarsMaud keeps drawing me calendars of coin. I keep telling her: the Ledger shows a profit. She keeps looking at me the way you look
